questions.stem: Calls arrive at 6 per hour. What is λ for a 20-minute window?
questions.incorrectFeedback: λ scales with the window: 6 per hour × (20/60) hour = 2.

questions.stem: X is Poisson with variance 3. What is E[X²]?
questions.correctFeedback: Yes — mean = variance = 3, and E[X²] = Var + mean² = 3 + 9 = 12.
questions.incorrectFeedback: For a Poisson the mean equals the variance, 3. Then E[X²] = Var(X) + (E[X])² = 3 + 9 = 12 (L7's shortcut, rearranged).

questions.stem: When is Poisson(np) a good stand-in for Bin(n, p)?
questions.correctFeedback: Correct — many trials, each rare. The variances npq and np then nearly agree.
questions.incorrectFeedback: It needs many trials and a small chance each: n large, p small. Then npq ≈ np, as for a Poisson.

questions.stem: From Lesson 8: a binomial has mean 6 and variance 4.2. What is p?
questions.incorrectFeedback: Divide variance by mean: q = npq/np = 4.2/6 = 0.7, so p = 1 − 0.7 = 0.3.

questions.incorrectFeedback: Use the complement: P(X = 0) = e^(−λ), so P(X ≥ 1) = 1 − e^(−λ). λe^(−λ) is P(X = 1) alone.
